title: First Conditional: If + Present, Will
grammarNote:
Первый условный (1st Conditional) — для РЕАЛЬНЫХ и ВОЗМОЖНЫХ ситуаций в будущем.

📌 Формула: IF + Present Simple → WILL + base verb
⚠️ В if-clause нет "will"! После "if" всегда Present Simple!

① Реальные будущие условия:
   "If I pass the exam, I will celebrate."
   "If she studies hard, she will get a good grade."
   "If it rains tomorrow, we will cancel the trip."

② Предупреждения:
   "If you don't hurry, you will miss the bus!"

③ Обещания:
   "If you help me, I will help you in return."

🔄 Порядок клауз — оба варианта правильны:
"If I study hard, I will pass." = "I will pass if I study hard."
Если IF-clause первый → запятая!

⚠️ Типичная ошибка:
❌ "If I will study, I will pass." → ✅ "If I study, I will pass."

grammarTip:
Главное правило — никогда "will" в if-клаузе!

❌ "If I WILL study, I will pass." (ОШИБКА!)
✅ "If I study, I will pass." (правильно)

Практика — исправь ошибки:
❌ "If she will call, I will answer." → ✅ "If she calls, I will answer."
❌ "If you will help me, I will be grateful." → ✅ "If you help me, I will be grateful."

exercises.text: If she studies hard, she ___ the exam.
If it rains, we ___ (cancel) the trip.
exercises.hint: First conditional result: will + base verb.

exercises.text: "If I will go, I will see her" is correct.
exercises.hint: Never use "will" in the if-clause. Correct: "If I go, I will see her."

exercises.text: Which is a correct first conditional?
opts: If you will come, I am happy.
If you come, I will be happy.
If you came, I will be happy.
If you come, I am happy.
exercises.correct: If you come, I will be happy.
exercises.hint: If + present simple, will + infinitive = first conditional.

exercises.text: I ___ (not pass) if I don't study.
If Amir doesn't practise, he ___ lose the match.
exercises.hint: If he doesn't practise → he WILL lose. Negative condition + positive result.

exercises.text: What will you do if you ___ (fail) the test?
exercises.hint: If-clause: present simple (no will). "fail" not "will fail".
First conditional = real future possibilities. Scientific truths = zero conditional.

exercises.text: In "If she practises, her English will improve," the if-clause uses present simple.
exercises.hint: "she practises" = present simple in the if-clause. Correct first conditional.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct negative form.
exercises.text: If we ___ (not hurry), we will miss the train.
exercises.hint: Negative if-clause: don't + base verb (present simple).

opts: If she practises, she will improve.
If she will practise, she improves.
She will improve if she will practise.
If she improves, she will practise.
exercises.correct: If she practises, she will improve.
exercises.hint: If-clause: present simple. Result clause: will + infinitive.

opts: Zero uses will; first uses present simple
Zero is for facts; first is for real future possibilities
Zero is for the past; first for the present
exercises.correct: Zero is for facts; first is for real future possibilities
exercises.hint: Zero = always true facts. First = possible future situations.

questions.hint: First conditional: if + present simple → will + infinitive (the result).

questions.text: If Kamila gets a scholarship, she ___ study in Germany.
questions.hint: First conditional result clause: will + infinitive.

questions.text: "If it will rain, we will stay inside" is correct.
questions.hint: Never use "will" in the if-clause. Correct: "If it rains, we will stay inside."

questions.text: If you don't hurry, you ___ miss the bus.
questions.hint: "If you don't hurry" = negative condition → "you will miss" = the result.

questions.text: We ___ (go) hiking if the weather is good.

opts: If you heat it, it melts.
If I had money, I would buy it.
If she studies, she will pass.
If I were you, I would help.
questions.correct: If she studies, she will pass.
questions.hint: If + present simple, will + infinitive = first conditional.

questions.text: If they ___ (not practise), they won't win.
questions.hint: If-clause: present simple, negative → don't practise.

questions.text: "I will help you if I finish early." — The if-clause is:
questions.hint: The if-clause introduces the condition. It can come at the end of the sentence.

questions.text: First conditional describes real, possible future situations.
questions.hint: Yes — first conditional is for situations that are genuinely possible.

questions.text: "If you don't eat breakfast, you ___ have energy." Fill in:
Zhibek says that if it is hot this summer, she will:
questions.hint: From the listening: Zhibek said "If it is hot, I will travel to the mountains."

questions.text: Rustam says that if his team wins, he will practise more.
questions.hint: Rustam said he will celebrate with friends if they win.

questions.text: Gulnaz uses the zero conditional when she says:
opts: If I get a scholarship, I will study abroad
If we practise every day, we will win
If you press the button, the machine starts
If it is hot, I will travel
questions.correct: If you press the button, the machine starts
questions.hint: Gulnaz used the zero conditional — present simple in both clauses.
"Possibility" = a chance that something may happen.

questions.text: A general ___ is a fact that is always true, like "water boils at 100°C".
questions.hint: A "truth" is something that is always correct — often expressed with zero conditional.

opts: A commitment to do something in the future
questions.correct: A commitment to do something in the future
questions.hint: A promise = a firm commitment to do something.
